Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)

Required findings: Patient must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608.

Imaging must demonstrate one of the following: degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis with dynamic segmental instability on flexion‑extension X‑rays or supine vs upright views showing >3 mm translational slip; Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis; isthmic spondylolisthesis with progression on plain films; multi‑level spondylolysis; postoperative facet disruption >50 % bilaterally or >75 % of a single facet; pars fracture; iatrogenic spondylolisthesis after prior decompression.

Documentation of nicotine‑free status: either never‑smoker or abstinent from all tobacco/nicotine products for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery, verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva).
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, opioid or alcohol use disorder).
Patient must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608.

Planned surgical technique must be expected to create instability, such as: facet joint excision >50 % bilaterally or >75 % of a single facet; pars interarticularis removal; decompression for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis; partial or complete corpectomy (removal of ≥1/3 vertebral body).
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as described above.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders.
Patient must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608.

Imaging must show either coronal plane deformity (Cobb angle >30°, asymmetric disc collapse causing symptomatic foraminal narrowing, or global coronal imbalance) OR sagittal imbalance (sagittal vertical axis >8 cm or pelvic incidence‑lumbar lordosis mismatch >15°).
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as described above.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders.
Medical necessity indications.Source: Section CMM-609.4 > Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity

Required findings: Patient must be a candidate for an initial primary lumbar discectomy per CMM-606.2.

Advanced imaging must demonstrate one of the following: primary extraforaminal L5‑S1 disc herniation where a far‑lateral approach is not feasible due to iliac wing; primary foraminal herniation requiring facet resection that would cause instability; or a disc herniation at the level of the conus medullaris.
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as described above.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders.
Patient must be a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM-606.3 at the same level.

Imaging must show anterolisthesis at the operative level with either dynamic instability on flexion‑extension X‑rays (or supine vs upright >3 mm translation) or Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as described above.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders.

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Second or Greater Recurrent Disc Herniation
Required findings: Patient must be a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM-606.3 at the same level.
No additional imaging criteria beyond those required for the initial repeat procedure; however nicotine‑free status and mental health criteria still apply.
Documentation of nicotine‑free status as described above.
Medical necessity indications.Source: Section CMM-609.4 > Second or Greater Recurrent Disc Herniation

Non-Indications: Percutaneous lumbar spinal fusion, endoscopic lumbar fusion, anterior laparoscopic interbody fusion, dynamic stabilization devices, interlaminar lumbar instrumented fusion, interspinous distraction/fixation devices, isolated facet fusion, and any fusion technique listed under the Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (EIU) category (Section CMM-609.9).
Lumbar fusion performed without meeting the specific criteria outlined in the General Guidelines or the procedure‑specific sections (Section CMM-609.9 – Not Medically Necessary).
Important criteria & exceptions: Nicotine‑free status must be documented either by self‑report of never‑smoking or by objective cotinine testing confirming abstinence for ≥6 weeks prior to surgery.
If intra‑operative findings reveal instability, the pre‑operative imaging criteria for instability are waived (exception noted in Actual Instability).

Urgent/emergent indications (e.g., traumatic fracture with instability, infection with instability, neoplastic pathologic fracture, or severe debilitating pain/incapacitation) do not require completion of conservative management, smoking cessation proof, or mental health clearance.
Documentation required: Recent flexion‑extension lumbar X‑rays or supine vs upright radiographs demonstrating translational slip >3 mm, or static imaging showing Meyerding grade ≥II spondylolisthesis.
MRI or CT reports confirming disc herniation characteristics, neural element compression, or deformity measurements (Cobb angle, sagittal vertical axis, pelvic incidence‑lumbar lordosis).
Objective cotinine test results (serum, urine, or saliva) confirming nicotine‑free status, or a signed statement of never‑smoker status.

Clinical notes documenting severity of pain, functional impairment, and failure of at least three months of conservative therapy (prescription analgesics, NSAIDs, gabapentinoids, steroids, and/or supervised physical therapy).
Mental health assessment confirming absence of unmanaged significant psychiatric or substance‑use disorders.
If applicable, operative reports from prior lumbar surgery demonstrating iatrogenic instability or hardware failure.
